findings.reason: this is the section's only bullet about the held-split case and the pass's actual writes turn on it, so a node reading one outcome and the coordinator reviewing the other would each be right about a different graph state.
findings.text: the changed exception says a §1 family the pass leaves undecided "is not written to one domain", while the paragraph above it and §5's ruling both say such a family is held split with "each member decided on its own sources"; a worker can satisfy the clause by leaving every member at its stored domain (nothing written) or by rewriting each member individually (a §5 judgment per member), and the two produce different stored domains and different judgment counts

findings.reason: a worker dispatched on §3 has to decide the placement itself and may run the live pass in place with no committed gate receipt, which is exactly what the named-partition and committed-log bullets exist to prevent.
findings.text: §3's done-when names no compute partition and requires no committed gate log, though the section writes the live graph over 1,247 families and takes a checkpoint before it, while §2's seventh bullet and §5's ninth both name a partition and a committed log

findings.reason: §3 is declared implementable behind an open gate whose condition has been met, so the section reads as blocked on a ruling already made and the gate's state, not the plan's content, would decide whether a node dispatches.
findings.text: gate g-sdpf-disputed-items gates §3 and still reads data-status="open" with no verdict, while its required evidence is satisfied on HEAD (docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-family-labels/disputed-items.json carries lead_ruling on all 12 items) and the ruling is recorded in the plan's own comment c-s5-lead-ruling-disputed-and-bound

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-per-family/ and docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-family-labels/disputed-items.json both exist at HEAD, sn-catalog-consistency §5 resolves and its metadata carries the declared wait on sn-domain-per-family#s3, and §5's widened-options.json listing (delivered at the §5 node's head d77fb15b, not yet on main) reports 24 undecided families of two or more members, matching the ruling §3 relies on.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §3's second done-when bullet (plan.html:71) admits two different graph outcomes for a §1 family the pass leaves undecided, because "is not written to one domain" does not say whether its members are left at their stored domains or rewritten individually as the ruling says.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §3 names docs/evidence/fragments/sn-domain-per-family/ as its evidence directory and that path resolves, but no bullet requires the pass's gate log committed there and no compute partition is named for a live-graph pass over 1,247 families, unlike §2's seventh bullet and §5's ninth.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §3 names no symbol, file of code or plan label, and its prose states mechanism rather than carrying a ticket reference.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §3's stated cause (a family offered only its sources' domains, then left undecided under the wider set) matches the shipped measurement, its endpoint is obtainable from the live graph, and the section prescribes no code path or formula.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 has one deliverable, the live names brought to one domain per family; its share, spend and audit bullets are measures of that one pass, not second deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — every depends-on and the g-sdpf-disputed-items relationship resolve correctly, but that gate is still open; that gate's required evidence is committed and the ruling is recorded, so §3 reads as gated on a ruling that has already been made.
